The '''2017–18 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arizona]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by ninth-year head coach [[Sean Miller]], and played their home games at [[McKale Center]] in [[Tucson, Arizona]] as members in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. They finished the season 27–8, 14–4 in [[2017–18 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to win the regular season championship. They defeated [[2017–18 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]], [[2017–18 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]], and [[2017–18 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] to win the [[2018 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]]. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where, as a No. 4 seed, they were upset in the first round by No. 13 seed [[2017–18 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]].

Due to [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]], 18 wins from this season have been vacated.<ref>{{cite web |title=IARP ruling a major victory for Wildcats, who avoid significant penalty in infractions case |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/iarp-ruling-a-major-victory-for-wildcats-who-avoid-significant-penalty-in-infractions-case/article_2a2aa186-7bd2-11ed-817a-1f1403b6aa36.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2017-18 Arizona Wildcat Basketball Season |url=https://stats.ncaa.org/teams/110949}}</ref>  The following 9 wins against [[2017–18 Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball team|Northern Arizona]], [[2017–18 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]], [[2017–18 Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners men's basketball team|Cal State Bakersfield]], [[2017–18 Long Beach State 49ers men's basketball team|Long Beach State]], [[2017–18 UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball team|UNLV]], [[2017–18 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], [[2017–18 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]], [[2017–18 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]] & [[2017–18 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] would count in the overall record as the player involved in the scandal did not play in these games.

==Previous season==
{{main|2016–17 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team}}

Entering the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]], Arizona had been ranked in 78 consecutive AP polls and 81-straight Coaches polls. The Wildcats were ranked every week extending their streak to 97 weeks for the AP and 100 weeks for the Coaches poll. The 97 consecutive weeks in the AP poll is currently the second-longest streak in the nation behind [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] at 161 weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/arizona.sidearmsports.com/documents/2016/10/26/Final_2016_17_Media_Guide_for_Online.pdf|title=Arizona Media Guide|website=ArizonaWildcats.com|access-date=27 January 2017}}</ref> Arizona won its first 10 conference games, the best start since the 1997–98 season when they started 16–0. During the season, Arizona was invited and participated in the [[Armed Forces Classic]] in [[Honolulu]]. Arizona defeated [[2016–17 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. Arizona also defeated [[2016–17 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the Lone Star Shootout in [[Houston]]. Arizona also defeated [[2016–17 Sacred Heart Pioneers men's basketball team|Sacred Heart]], [[2016–17 Northern Colorado Bears men's basketball team|Northern Colorado]] and [[2016–17 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team|Santa Clara]] but lost to [[2016–17 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] in the championship game of the [[Las Vegas Invitational]] in [[Paradise, Nevada|Paradise, NV]].

They finished the season 32–5, 16–2 in [[2016–17 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in a first place tie with [[2016–17 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]]. The championship marked the school's 15th Pac-12 regular season championship title. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], Arizona defeated [[2016–17 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]], [[2016–17 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] and [[2016–17 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] (avenged from 85 to 58 loss on February 4 in Eugene, OR) to win the sixth Pac-12 tournament championship title since 2002. As a result, the Wildcats received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the fifth consecutive year (32nd NCAA tournament appearances). As a No. 2 seed in the West region, they defeated [[2016–17 North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball team|North Dakota]] 100–82 and [[2016–17 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]] 69–60 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. However, in the Sweet Sixteen, they lost to No. 11 seed [[2016–17 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] 73–71.

===2017 recruiting class===
[[Tempe, Arizona]] product [[Alex Barcello]] was the first commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on August 26 at a press conference at his high school. He chose Arizona over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]. He was a consensus four star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 93 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

[[Deandre Ayton]], a [[The Bahamas|Bahamian]] attending school in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], was the second commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on September 6 live on [[ESPN]]. He chose Arizona for an upset over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats basketball|Kentucky]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 2 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

Brandon Randolph, originally from [[Yonkers, New York]], was the third commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on October 12. He chose Arizona over [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]]. He was a consensus top fifty player, ranked No. 42 by the four main recruiting services.

Ira Lee, from [[Los Angeles]], was the fourth commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on October 20. He chose Arizona over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and Oregon. He was a consensus top-25 player and ranked as a four-star player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 24/7 Sports.

[[Emmanuel Akot]] from [[Winnipeg]], [[Canada|CA]], was the first commitment in the 2018 Arizona class, but he will [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to 2017 class (fifth and final commitment). He committed to Arizona on March 9 at a press conference at his high school. He chose Arizona over [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], Oregon and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 21 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

Arizona also added [[Walk-on (sports)|Preferred Walk-on]] Matt Weyand from [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] in [[Santa Ana, California]].

==FBI investigation==

On February 23, 2018, according to a published report by ESPN, an FBI wiretap revealed that head coach [[Sean Miller]] talked with Christian Dawkins (another key figure in the scandal) to discuss paying their top prospect, [[Deandre Ayton]], $100,000 to commit to Arizona, with the monetary situation being dealt with directly with him.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22559284/sean-miller-arizona-christian-dawkins-discussed-payment-ensure-deandre-ayton-signing-according-fbi-investigation |title=FBI wiretaps show Sean Miller discussed $100K payment to lock recruit |last=Schlabach |first=Mark |date=February 23, 2018 |website=www.espn.com |publisher=ESPN |access-date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> While Miller would not coach their next game that day against Oregon, Arizona allowed Ayton to play.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22567552/sean-miller-coach-arizona-wildcats-saturday-oregon-ducks |title=Sean Miller won't coach Arizona's game Saturday vs. Oregon|date=February 24, 2018 |website=www.espn.com |publisher=ESPN |access-date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> Coach Sean Miller subsequently denied the allegation and the University of Arizona announced he will remain the coach of Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team, with Ayton also allowed to continue playing with the team for the rest of the season. However, as a consequence of the report involving Ayton, both of Arizona's remaining committed recruits from the class of 2018, [[Shareef O'Neal]] and Brandon Williams, announced they had decommitted.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/03/sean-miller-deandre-ayton-arizona-nba-draft|title = Sean Miller: Deandre Ayton will declare for NBA draft}}</ref>

== Preseason ==

=== Summer Exhibition Tour ===
Practices began earlier than otherwise allowed by the NCAA in preparation for a three-game foreign tour to Spain in August. (NCAA rules allow teams to conduct 10 practices in preparation for a foreign tour.) NCAA rules allow for foreign tours once every four years and the Spain tour was Arizona's first since 2012.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://tucson.com/sports/basketball/college/wildcats/arizona-basketball-bahamas-trip-gives-cats-time-to-mesh/article_82229b3f-d9bf-59c6-9964-81ac04fd6fe2.html|title=Arizona basketball: Bahamas trip gives Cats time to mesh|last=Star|first=Bruce Pascoe Arizona Daily|work=Arizona Daily Star|access-date=2017-06-14|language=en}}</ref> It was the eighth in program history. The University of Arizona basketball program will travel to Spain in August for a foreign tour, including a trio of exhibition games. The Wildcats will spend time in Barcelona and Valencia Aug. 11 through Aug. 19.

UA will take on Combinado Valenciano on Saturday, Aug. 13 at 7 p.m. local at the Pabellon Municipal Fuente de San Luis in Valencia.

The trip's second exhibition features Arizona and the Mataro All-Stars on Wednesday, August 16 at 7:10 p.m. in Barcelona inside the Pavello Municipal Teresa Maria Roca prior to the final exhibition two days later against Mataro Parc Boet in the same arena.

All three of the exhibitions will be streamed online by FloHoops.com with a subscription required.

=== Red and Blue game ===
The annual Red-Blue game will take place at McKale Center on October 20, 2017. After freshman Brandon Randolph won the dunk contest,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2017/10/20/16512542/arizona-red-blue-game-dunk-contest-highlights-deandre-ayton-brandon-randolph-ira-lee-pinder-barcello|title=Brandon Randolph wins Red-Blue Game dunk contest|last=Kelapire|first=Ryan|date=20 October 2017|website=AZDesertSwarm.com|access-date=20 October 2017}}</ref> the Blue team, led by Deandre Ayton, knocked off the Red team, 55–37.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2017/10/20/16512550/arizona-basketball-red-blue-game-recap-deandre-ayton-brandon-randolph-final-score-stats-highlights|title=Deandre Ayton, Brandon Randolph shine in Arizona's Red-Blue Game|last=Kelapire|first=Ryan|date=20 October 2017|website=AZDesertSwarm.com|access-date=20 October 2017}}</ref>
